items.title: Show HN: Pulse Local, a Mac budgeting app whose AI models run on your machine
items.author: niztk
items.text:
Hi HN, I'm Niz. Pulse Local is a budgeting app for Mac (Apple Silicon, beta) that answers questions about your spending with models that run on your machine. Local mode needs no account. The ledger and your questions stay on the machine, and the app sends no analytics or crash logs.

I felt there are not enough consumer apps that run locally with no calls to the outside world that help us manage sensitive corners of our lives. This app in its local variant only downloads a couple of models
items.summary: Pulse Local is a budgeting app for Mac that runs AI models locally on the user's machine, offering a complete budgeting experience without requiring an account. The app ensures that the ledger and questions stay on the machine and sends no analytics or crash logs. It features an assistant built on a fine-tuned model and thousands of rules embedded in the code. The app is available for free with options to support further development. The app's local mode emphasizes privacy and control over financial data, running models locally to avoid cloud-based costs and data sharing.

items.title: 900-Page Pre-Pantone Guide to Color from 1692 (With Complete High-Res Scan)
items.author: mdp2021
items.summary: The sources describe a 900-page book titled Traité des couleurs servant à la peinture à l’eau, also known as Klaer Lightende Spiegel der Verfkonst, created by Dutch artist A. Boogert in 1692. This book, which predates the Pantone system, features over 700 pages of color swatches and was recently discovered in the archives of the Bibliothèque Méjanes in Aix-en-Provence, France, by Medieval book historian Erik Kwakkel. The complete high-resolution digital scan of the book is now available online.

items.title: The United Kingdom generates less electricity per person than in the 1970s
items.author: karakoram
items.summary: The United Kingdom generates less electricity per person today than in the 1970s. According to Our World in Data, electricity generation per person peaked in 2003 at about 6,700 kWh and has since fallen by more than a third to about 4,200 kWh in the latest year, lower than the roughly 4,300 kWh recorded in 1968. Internet Geography also notes that today, the UK consumes less energy than it did in 1970, with household energy use decreasing by 12 percent and heavy industry seeing a 60 percent decline. The decline in electricity consumption is attributed to factors such as deindustrialization, higher electricity prices, lower economic growth, and a shift towards a less energy-intensive service-based economy.

items.title: Apple's new 'Switch to Safari' campaign details why you should ditch Chrome
items.author: ivell
items.summary: Apple is launching a new campaign to promote Safari’s benefits over Chrome, highlighting better battery life, stronger privacy protections, and faster performance. The campaign includes a new “Switch to Safari” page and YouTube videos that claim Safari offers up to 5 hours more video streaming on Mac compared with Chrome, stronger privacy protections, and is up to 35% faster than Chrome when loading frequently visited sites on Mac. The campaign emphasizes Safari’s design to work specifically with Apple hardware for performance advantages.

items.title: OpenAI engineer arrested in bugging of executive conference room
items.author: forthwall
items.summary: An OpenAI engineer, Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested on suspicion of secretly installing a recording device in a conference room used by company executives at its San Francisco headquarters. Federal prosecutors charged Alfozan with using or attempting to use a device to intercept oral communications. The device was found plugged into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room and had been concealed in toilet paper. Alfozan, a Saudi national who joined the company last year, appeared in federal court and remained in custody.

items.title: Maybe a better way to track the release history of a Git repo
items.author: evakhoury
items.summary: To track the release history of a Git repository, one proposed method involves using a special ref named `HISTORY` that points to a metainfo commit containing release information. This method uses commands like `git log --reverse --format="%P %cd" HISTORY` to access the release commit and `git fetch origin refs/release/stg.www.our-app:HISTORY` to set up the tracking. After fetching, `git log HISTORY` lists the release history in reverse chronological order, and `git log -1 --until=date HISTORY` can find the last release before a certain date. Another approach is using `git log` to view commit history in reverse chronological order, showing author, date, and commit hash. Additionally, tools like `logbook` can provide structured events and a hero's journey narrative of the repo's history.

items.title: Hiking the world in search of rare cheeses
items.author: tosh
items.summary: Trevor Warmedahl, a former commercial cheesemaker from Seattle, embarked on a global journey to discover traditional cheesemaking methods after realizing he was using milk from animals he never saw. Over the past six years, he has traveled through more than 20 countries, documenting traditional cheesemaking and pastoral lifestyles, and offering workshops on natural dairy processing. His adventures have taken him to places like Bulgaria, Pakistan, Italy, Austria, and Cambodia. The BBC article highlights his belief that "cheese is an edible manifestation of a place," and his recent 193km trek across the Peaks of the Balkans Trail. The Hacker News discussion mentions a cheese from the Himalayan region of South Asia reputed to be the "hardest cheese in the world," and a Corsican cheese called Casu martzu. The YouTube video discusses the Salers Tradition, a rare farmhouse cheese from France, and the near-extinction of the Salers cattle breed.

items.title: How Do Cuttlefish Hide?
items.author: marojejian
items.summary: Cuttlefish hide from enemies using camouflage and clouds of ink. They can change skin color, pattern, and texture almost instantly through a combination of chromatophores, iridophores, and papillae. They can also release ink to create a "smoke screen" for evasion. In addition, small male cuttlefish can hide their sexually dimorphic fourth arms and mimic the appearance of nonreceptive females to deceive guarding males.

items.title: The Feeling of Power
items.author: layer8
items.summary: "The Feeling of Power" is a science fiction short story by Isaac Asimov that first appeared in the February 1958 issue of If: Worlds of Science Fiction and was later reprinted in various collections. The story explores themes of technological deskilling and human dependence on automation, cautioning against human mental atrophy in the computer era. The protagonist, Aub, develops a method for rapid multiplication but commits suicide when he sees his discovery used for military purposes. The story has been cited as an early exploration of these themes, which later became associated with calculators, GPS navigation, and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Show HN: Parsimony – an open-source benchmark for how much code AI models add
items.author: lasu
items.text:
Existing benchmarks measure solve rate and token output/cost, but don't punish excess code, which makes a codebase harder to work with in the long term. I wanted to measure this since it matters most for long-term projects.

Method: it takes the patches that benchmarks already publish (DeepSWE, SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Live) and counts "coding units": syntax elements like statements, calls, names and literals. I didn't use lines of code, so cramming code isn't
items.summary: Parsimony is an open-source benchmark that measures how much code AI models add by counting "coding units" such as statements, calls, comparisons, names, and literals, rather than lines of code. It subtracts deleted code to measure net units, thus avoiding rewarding cramming code. The benchmark uses patches from existing benchmarks like DeepSWE and counts coding units to evaluate AI models. As of the latest data, models like Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, Claude Fable 5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and others have been evaluated, with specific coding unit counts and success rates provided. Notably, GPT-5.6 Sol's private run added 0.88× the code of its published run.

items.title: How to engineer an AI harness for game development
items.author: kkukshtel
items.summary: To engineer an AI harness for game development, focus on modular design and extensibility, as many modern harnesses are modular and can plug in or toggle components. The harness should handle the non-deterministic nature of AI, manage AI-specific limitations like token limits or hallucinations, and incorporate prompt design, tool APIs, and UX design for how the AI interacts. The harness connects the model to tools, systems, memory, and execution environments to carry out actions, and it is designed to handle unexpected behaviors gracefully.

items.title: AI is a tool and using it well takes skill
items.author: layer8
items.summary: The sources emphasize that AI is a tool that requires skill to use effectively. According to Stewart, mastery of AI skills involves familiarity with industry-specific tools and understanding the broader context of AI for leadership roles. Data Mind highlights that extraordinary results from AI come from using the same tools differently, attributing success to five skills rather than the number of tools used. Frank Elavsky argues against the simplistic view that AI is just a tool, stressing the importance of ethical considerations in its use.

items.title: Maybe a better way to track the release history of a Git repo
items.author: hellerve
items.summary: To track the release history of a Git repository, the sources suggest using `git log --reverse --format="%P %cd" HISTORY` to access the current release commit and metainfo commit from previous releases. The metainfo commit is stored in a reference named `stg.www.our-app` which contains metadata like the treesha. To list the entire release history in reverse chronological order, `git fetch origin refs/release/stg.www.our-app:HISTORY` followed by `git log HISTORY` can be used. Additionally, `git tag` is recommended for tagging commits with version numbers and generating build artifacts. The GitHub project logbook also provides a method to turn Git history into memory for AI coding agents.

items.title: Worlds more habitable than Earth?
items.author: cainxinth
items.summary: The sources suggest that a superhabitable planet is one that might have an even better chance at hosting life than Earth due to various factors. These include a larger size and mass, which could provide more habitable surface area and a thicker, more stable atmosphere. Planets with about 1.5 times Earth's mass could retain their interior heat longer, keeping their core molten and protective magnetic field active for a longer period. Additionally, planets with smaller continents might be more habitable than those with large, interior deserts. Planets slightly warmer than Earth on a billion-year timescale may also be superhabitable due to larger tropical zones that could support more biodiversity. However, planets substantially warmer than Earth could have oxygen-depleted oceans. The sources do not provide definitive details on specific planets or exact conditions.

items.title: Creating a Garmin "MCP"
items.author: ricotico060
items.summary: To create a Garmin MCP, you can use open source projects like runningworkout.fr which is free and more secure, or paid solutions like pulsai.me. The Garmin Workouts MCP server allows you to create Garmin Connect workouts using natural language descriptions. To install, use the command `claude mcp add garmin-workouts-mcp npx garmin-workouts-mcp` for the recommended Claude Code. For MCPCursor, create a `.env` file with `GARMIN_EMAIL` and `GARMIN_PASSWORD`, generate a token with `python example.py`, and register the MCP server in Claude Desktop with `mcp install garmin_mcp_server.py`. Garmin's auth tokens expire every ~5 minutes, so plan multiple workouts in one session.

items.title: IDRs as Records of Intent
items.author: evakhoury
items.summary: The sources indicate that IDRs (Implementation Decision Records) serve to improve the output of LLMs and provide a durable record of decisions made during feature implementation. However, they are not very effective as records of intent when left to their own devices, as LLMs tend to generate descriptions of planned implementations rather than clear intents. For IRS Information Document Requests (IDRs), they are used by the IRS to request documents or pose questions to taxpayers to understand relevant facts or positions, and maintaining a robust record of IDR responses can help taxpayers identify trends in an audit team’s process and prepare for Appeals or litigation. The IDR process involves issuing requests that encourage collaboration between taxpayers and IRS personnel to provide needed information.
